releases.name: DSH plugin 1.2.34 (overlay 1.0.21)
releases.body:
The DSH bundle for overlay 1.0.21. It carries the same panel binary and `protocol.js` as the release; the only change on this line is the vendored overlay, which now contains the window-procedure guard described in the 1.0.21 notes.

Detail: https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

releases.name: AI Terminal Pet 1.0.21
releases.body:
A process that stays alive with a window that never answers is worse than a crash: nothing is logged, nothing restarts, and the machine just looks broken. One did that here for hours. The UI thread had hit a fatal panic inside a window procedure, and the runtime's fatal printer then deadlocked on a lock held by a goroutine it had just frozen - so it never exited, and the panic text went to the stderr the reporter launches us with and ignores.

Both window procedures now run through one guarded entry: a panic is recovered, written to `error.log` with its message and stack, and the overlay closes cleanly if it happens three times. Nested message dispatch is capped at 64 and the refusal is logged once - the thread stack in the dump was 1.8 MB of nested user32 send-message frames against a 2 MB reserve.

The animations switch from the previous round ships in the same batch: the waiting/error breath is the only thing that moves, and `animations=off` freezes it without removing any state colour or glyph. The catalogue text now says what installation actually is: DeepSeek Harness on install, OpenCode one command, Claude Code and Antigravity a reporter each.

Detail: https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

releases.name: dsh-ai-terminal-pet 1.2.33
releases.body:
Bundled overlay: 1.0.20, and one behaviour change: the OpenCode reporter package now carries this same panel, so `opencode plugin add opencode-ai-terminal-pet` installs the overlay too. Nothing in the bundle itself changed beyond the vendored binary and the shared `protocol.js`.

Detail: https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

releases.name: AI Terminal Pet 1.0.20
releases.body:
opencode plugin add opencode-ai-terminal-pet is now the whole installation on Windows. The package carries the panel and puts it in place on first load - verified against its own manifest, through a temp file and a rename, never overwriting a panel you already have. 1.0.19 wired the reporter and left you to install the app separately; measured against what people actually do, that was a dead end: no panel appeared and nothing said why.

Linux and macOS deliberately stay two steps: a single binary is not an install there (autostart entry, reporters, uninstall record), so those platforms use the release tarball and `install.sh`, and both the package README and `--doctor` say so.

Nothing in the panel itself changed; this release exists because the vendored binary embeds the overlay's version, and the reporter is versioned with it.

Detail: https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

releases.name: dsh-ai-terminal-pet 1.2.32
releases.body:
Bundled overlay: 1.0.19. The bundle's own behaviour is unchanged - this release exists because the overlay version is compiled into the binary it vendors.

1.0.19 fixes `--doctor` on machines that installed the OpenCode reporter with `opencode plugin add`: the check looked in the config directory, the CLI installs into `~/.cache/opencode/npm/...`, and a correct install therefore got a warning. See the release notes for the overlay line.

Detail: https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
